children: The Canadian GDP is expected to have expanded by 0.2% from the previous month in August 2026, according to a flash estimate.
Growth is set to be driven by gains in mining and quarrying and retail trade, partly offset by declines in oil and gas extraction.
The figure follows a flat reading in July, in line with market expectations, following three consecutive months of growth.

The goods-producing sector, which contrbutes roughly a quarter of the GDP, was essentially unchanged in July, as increases in construction (1.3%) and utilities (1.7%) were offset by declines in manufacturing (-0.9%) and mining, quarrying and oil and gas (-0.5%).

Simultaneously, the services-producing industries aggregate remained flat, as increases in sectors such as professional, scientific and technical services (0.3%); real estate and rental and leasing (0.2%) and accommodation and food services (0.8%) were offset by declines in retail trade (-1%) and wholesale trade (-0.4%).

title: Canada GDP Set to Rise Slightly in August
